episodes.title: Two Signup Paths. One Real Question.

experiment.assignment_note: Three videos per variant across three topic families. Observational matched batch, not a randomized causal test.

episodes.premise: A fictional adult folds two paper doors, then writes what she actually came to do on a tiny shopping list.
episodes.payoff: A purpose note turns an abstract account choice into a concrete reading task.
episodes.narration: Which door matches why you came here? A fictional scene. Mira folds two paper doors, then notices her tiny shopping list. Atomy’s U.S. guide separates consumer and distributor registration. The distributor path includes Social Security and bank information. She puts the list between the doors. First name your purpose. Then read the matching path. The official guide is in the caption.

episodes.title: One Card Was Missing From Her Checklist

experiment.assignment_note: Three videos per variant across three topic families. Observational matched batch, not a randomized causal test.

episodes.premise: A fictional adult arranges a self-made checklist; a blank gap leads her back to the official guide.

episodes.narration: What did her neat little checklist leave out? A fictional scene. Mira lines up three cards. The empty space bothers her, so she opens the source. Atomy’s U.S. registration guide requires a sponsor and describes automatic or manual designation. She adds a fourth card: understand the sponsor step. A tidy summary can still miss a decision. The official guide is in the caption.

episodes.title: She Nearly Folded Away the Useful Number

experiment.assignment_note: Three videos per variant across three topic families. Observational matched batch, not a randomized causal test.

episodes.premise: A fictional adult almost folds a paper comparison above its final-cost row, then unfolds it into a useful shopping tool.
episodes.payoff: The dramatic paper reveal exposes a useful comparison criterion, not a fabricated discount.
episodes.narration: Which number was she about to fold away? A fictional scene. Mira circles a price, then notices the bottom of her comparison sheet. The FTC recommends comparing product details and the full cost, including delivery and other fees. She unfolds the page. Atomy or another shop: match the item, check the size, then compare the total. The shopping guide is in the caption.

episodes.title: Three Boxes Before the Buy Button

experiment.assignment_note: Three videos per variant across three topic families. Observational matched batch, not a randomized causal test.

episodes.premise: A fictional adult arranges three clear comparison boxes beside a shopping card and discovers why an attractive price alone is incomplete.
episodes.payoff: Blank comparison boxes turn an incomplete shopping impression into an explicit checklist.
episodes.narration: Exact item. Size. Total cost. Three checks before a price comparison. A fictional scene. Jon lays three empty boxes beside a shopping card. The bold price leaves questions unanswered. FTC shopping guidance says to compare product details and include delivery and other fees. Atomy or another shop, he completes the comparison before choosing. The empty boxes were the useful part. The shopping guide is in the caption.
